To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the addition of diglycerides to microsomes from aged rat brain restores the decreased synthesis of choline and ethanol-amine phosphoglyceride in brain membranes.
the addition of diglyceride to microsomes from aged rats restores the activity of phospholipid biosynthesis.
the addition of diglycerides to microsomal membranes obtained from aged rats practically restores decreased phospholipid synthesis in these membranes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of aging on brain microsomal phospholipid synthesis, and the effects of polyunsaturated lipids on the synthesis of phospholipids in brain microsomes of young and aged animals.
the effect of polyunsaturated lipids on the synthesis of phospholipids in brain microsomes during aging.
the effect of polyunsaturated fatty acid on the brain lipid synthesis during senescence.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

polyunsaturated phospholipid diglycerides can be considered as an important factor in the maintenance of membrane fluidity and in the regulation of the synthesis of choline and ethanolamines phosphoglycerides in the brain of aging rats.
the addition of diglycerides to brain microsomal preparations from aged rats restores the synthesizing activity of phospholipids.

the decrease of brain phospholipid synthesis in aged rats is not a consequence of the decrease of the activity of phospholipid synthesizing enzymes, but rather the result of an alteration of the properties of the microsomal membrane.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the addition of phospholipid to the microsomal membranes restores the decreased synthesising activity of choline and ethanolamines.
the decrease in the synthesizing activity of phosphatidylserine, phosphatidylglycerol and phosphatidylinositol during aging is due to an age-related change in the membrane structure.
the decreased synthesis of phosphoglycerides in the brain of old rats is probably caused by a decrease in the availability of diglycerides.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the addition of diglycerides to microsomal membranes can increase the activity of phosphatidyl choline and phosphatidyl ethanolamine synthesis.

the addition of phosphatidyl choline to microsomal preparations of aged rats is a promising method of restoring the decreased activity of choline and ethanolamines phosphoglyceride synthesizing enzymes in brain membranes.
the addition of polyunsaturated lipids to membranes of aged animals may have a significant influence on the synthesis of phospholipids and, therefore, on the metabolism of brain cells.
